annotations.text:
van-core web panel, 390pt phone portrait.

Instrument-dark: warm near-black, amber reserved for the inverter, green for harvest, blue for the alternator, red only for genuine alarms. Space Grotesk + IBM Plex Mono.

Rule the layout follows: the panel answers 'is the inverter on, and why' before anything else.

The energy graph is generated from a simulated 24h, not invented shapes - net line = in minus out, SOC integrates net, the duty figures match the ribbons, and the generator refuses to emit a series that would clip outside the axis it labels.

Cooking spikes dwarf the fridge on a linear axis, which is honest. That is why the inverter/compressor ribbons sit under the axis: duty cycle is the project's open question (CLAUDE.md 8.4) and it lives there, not in the areas.

Nothing here stores history yet. ESPHome web_server v3 charts are live-only, and the microSD logger from Phase 1 is not written.

Everything else on these screens maps to entities that already exist in nodes/van-core.yaml - the 14 number tunables, the arbiter flags, the fbot sensors.

Fail-safe states are the reason this panel exists at all.

01 and 02 are 'fails toward powered' - the inverter is on and the panel says why in red, so a forced-on state can never be mistaken for normal operation.

04 and 05 are the same coast machinery with two different triggers. 06 never touches the DC rail.

Power flow answers 'where is every watt going' without arithmetic: solar and engine in on the left, AC and DC out on the right, battery in the middle. Symbols carry the identity - sun, vehicle, sine, DC bars - so the values read at a glance.

Link thickness scales with power and a dead path goes thin and dashed, so a silently failed alternator charger reads instantly - exactly the failure the Phase 4 cabin display exists to catch.

The red outer arc is the bottom 20%: reserve, not capacity.
